title: Character art profile
description: One file per playable character, scripts/lora/characters/<id>.json: the state of that character's art, from the design lock to the installed tile. Scripts read the keys marked 'read by'; everything else is the record a later session needs. A new profile comes from `python scripts/lora/new_profile.py <id> --trigger <word>`, never from copying another character's file (his rule, 2026-10-13). Checked by `python scripts/lora/check_profile.py <id>`. The method is docs/CHARACTER_ART.md; the step skills are charlora, kitart and artinstall.

id.description: The character id, the same as data/characters/<id>.json. Read by every script.

trigger.description: The LoRA trigger word, <id>toll by convention (duketoll, lyratoll). Read by stage_dataset.py (captions) and test_checkpoints.py.

face_ref.description: File name in ComfyUI input/ of the face-only crop of the locked design, used at IP-Adapter PLUS FACE 0.6 (step 1). A full image bleeds costume and background in. Read by gen_candidates.py and test_checkpoints.py.

identity.description: The full-body identity prompt: quality tags, 1girl|1boy, solo, age, build, hair, eyes, every garment and its colour, weighted on the defining words. No expression (that lives in the shot). stage_dataset.py reads '1boy' from it to pick the caption subject. Read by gen_candidates.py.

identity_upper.description: The identity prompt with the lower-body garments removed, for 1024x1024 close-ups; naming trousers in a head shot makes the model cram in a whole body, often two. Read by gen_candidates.py.

negative_extra.description: Appended to common.NEG_BASE for this character: the looks it must not drift to (child, teenager, the wrong garment colours, thighhighs). Read by gen_candidates.py.

body_shots.description: The full-body dataset slots as [slug, clause] or [slug, clause, flag] rows; flag is 'noref' (no face reference) or 'back' (no face reference, the drawn back skeleton). Ruling #186: about a third of these are action shots (a lunge, a sprint, a strike, a turn, a crouch), each different, and the calm front-facing standing figure is a few slots, never the set. Read by gen_candidates.py.

items.description: clause: framing, pose, expression, hood state; written from what the image should show

face_shots.description: The close-up slots as [slug, clause] rows: facing, head turn, expression. Read by gen_candidates.py.

style.description: Overrides the style tail of the dataset prompt (default in gen_candidates.py). Read by gen_candidates.py.

out_dir.description: ComfyUI output folder for candidates (default lora_<id>). Read by gen_candidates.py.

dataset_name.description: The staging folder name for this dataset version (default <id>_v1). A new version gets a new name so earlier sets are never overwritten. Read by stage_dataset.py.

batch.description: Images per slot (default 4). Read by gen_candidates.py.

seed_offset.description: Bump to re-roll a slot with fresh seeds (default 0). Read by gen_candidates.py.

hand_fix.description: The 512px hand pass on body shots (default false). One job per image. OFF for brown skin: it painted pale glowing hands on Duke. Read by gen_candidates.py.

face_hand_fix.description: The hand pass on close-ups too (default false; Duke's head shots came back with burnt neon skin with it on). Read by gen_candidates.py.

hand_extra.description: Extra prompt for the hand pass. Read by gen_candidates.py.

hood_down_negative.description: Negative added only to shots whose clause says 'hood down' (Sara). Read by gen_candidates.py.

hood_default.description: The hood state the LoRA should assume when a prompt does not name one; every shot still names it (CHARACTER_ART.md step 1).

design_note.description: The locked look in prose: every garment and colour, hood state, age, build, what is banned. Written at the design lock (step 0).

approved_refs.description: Older profiles (Lyra, Sara v1): the approved reference images by path, before `approved` carried captions.

lock.description: The design lock record: when, how he chose (option labels are Claude's wording, his selections), the face source file, what was fixed in code. Null until he locks.

approved.description: The approved dataset images by his number: { "E3": { "file": "<output path>", "caption": "<caption as corrected by him>" } }. Written after the caption gate (step 1). Older profiles hold a plain string or a file-only object per number.

dataset.description: Where the staged dataset lives and what is in it (count, versions, backups).

training.description: The training run record: the run name, images, recipe (always the frozen one), start and finish, where the checkpoints and test sheets are.

lora.description: The installed LoRA file name in ComfyUI models/loras (<id>_toll.safetensors), with a note when a version was superseded. Written when he picks the step (step 2).

lora_checkpoint.description: The step he picked. 2000 for the final save, which has no step number in its file name.

lora_pick.description: His pick in his words, and what Claude recommended, so the next session knows they differed if they did.

lora_use.description: How to prompt this LoRA, learned from the checkpoint tests: the prompt shape that works (short plain, or the weighted identity), what to always state, what to add to the negative, what to watch for. Read by a session before any kit art. Null until the LoRA exists.

art_direction.description: His direction for the kit art: the aura colour in his words, his pose ideas per slot, his picks per round. Null until he has given any.

kit_art.description: The kit-art record: the slot plan he approved, his draft picks per slot, the official render method and the chosen renders, what is locked, what is installed.

portrait.description: The portrait crop record: the source cut-out and the make_portrait_crop.py numbers, so a sharper source reuses the framing (step 6).

tile.description: The tile crop record: the source cut-out, where the headroom stops and why, the TILE_ART ratio, the ART_VERSION bump (step 6).

status.description: Free text for a character that is held or mid-step: what was rendered, what is not reviewed, what needs options before the next batch.
